decisions_this_run: D-063a: derive risk from the capability in code, never from a model. A risk figure that sets an approval threshold is authority, and section 10 forbids a model from widening its own. Pure, total, deterministic, I/O-free, TypeError on a non-Capability rather than coercion.

D-063b: the tier floor can only RAISE the threshold. `min(2, max(1, policy, floor))`. A silent policy must not be able to reduce a high-risk action to one signature - the control that requests a protection must not define it away. Same rule step-up follows.

D-063c: risk is not a rename of SENSITIVE_CAPABILITIES. The tier separates those four by what they can destroy or expose, and a test asserts every sensitive capability is at least elevated so the two sets cannot drift into disagreement about danger.

D-063d: test the high-risk floor as a pure function rather than through the gateway. org_search is non-delegable, so no agent token can reach it; writing a gateway test would have required inventing a path that must not exist. Every other tier is exercised through the real gateway.

D-063e: keep the high-risk tier despite having no production caller. It is the correct answer the day a future ADR permits delegated org-wide search - the control exists before the capability that needs it. Documented as an explicit honest limit, not left implicit.
D-063f: clamp to the closed 1..2 vocabulary rather than returning 3 for high risk. ApprovalRequest models only 1 or 2; a value no code path can satisfy would be a lie on the record.
run_summary: NEX-063 closes the last named ADR-015 obligation. Approval existed, but its threshold was only what a policy author wrote, so a lockout-prone action and a routine read shared the same human gate - 'risk-based' was a name without a mechanism. Risk is now a pure function from capability to a closed ordered tier, and the gateway raises the signature count to the max of the policy threshold and the tier floor, clamped to 1..2. The decisive choice was to make risk code rather than a model score: a risk figure that sets an approval threshold is authority, and section 10 forbids a model from widening its own. The design also refuses to let a silent policy weaken a high-risk action, mirroring step-up's rule that the control which requests a protection cannot define it away. The honest limit is recorded rather than hidden: org_search is the only high-risk capability and it is non-delegable, so the two-signature floor has no production caller and is tested as a pure function; every other tier runs through the real gateway. All gates green on the committed tree - ruff format and check clean, mypy clean across 140 files, 1432 passed / 4 skipped, and 25 new tests. The clone started on main while the feature branch carried 60+ commits of prior work, so the remote tip was read from git ls-remote and the slice committed on top of it, avoiding a push that would have looked like a rewrite. Status is IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, COMMITTED, PUSHED - deliberately not VERIFIED, because CI has not been polled for this head.
